transcript:
Header:
- Date/Time: 2025-10-07 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~45 mins
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendoza (CTO, MedSphere), Aisha Rahman (Lead ML Engineer), Evan Price (DevOps), Nina Patel (PM)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: quick walkthrough of org/project keys and rate limits, answered security Qs, agreed next steps to share docs and start POC.
Topics: rate limits, org keys, quotas, security/compliance, POC next steps.
Action items: see metadata above.

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
00:00 Jordan Lee: All right hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood uh AE, and with me is Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Carlos Mendoza: Hi, thanks Jordan, doing well. We just got out of another meeting, so apologies if we're a little late.
00:12 Priya Nair: No worries, Carlos. We'll jump right in. Today we're going to demo the Console and the API flows for org/project keys and rate limiting, and show how you can set per-tenant quotas.
00:25 Aisha Rahman: Sounds good, high level we want per-customer quotas and the ability to throttle bursts — our main concerns are noisy tenants and cost control, also auditability.
00:36 Jordan Lee: Totally, that's exactly what we'll target. Quick intro: MedSphere was flagged as a mid-enterprise healthcare customer, interested in hosted but may need Private for data policies?
00:45 Carlos Mendoza: Correct. We're evaluating hosted first but we have regulatory pushes, so we need to understand VPC and KMS options and how RBAC ties to our SSO.
00:55 Priya Nair: We'll cover the KMS/HSM integration notes in the security pack, but for the demo we'll focus on rate limiting policies and org/project keys.
01:05 Jordan Lee: Priya, can you share your screen?
01:09 Speaker 2 (Priya shares): Yep, sharing now. Can folks see the Redwood Console? (brief pause)
01:20 Nina Patel: Yes we can. The Console looks clean.
01:23 Priya Nair: Great. So top-level concept: you create an organization, then projects under orgs. Each project gets API keys (project keys) and you can bind rate limit policies at org or project level.
01:35 Priya Nair: Here is an example policy: steady_rate 20 r/s, burst 200 tokens per minute, and per-day quota of 5M tokens. You can also attach usage alarms and webhooks to notify when thresholds are near.
01:48 Aisha Rahman: Sorry can you repeat the units, r/s vs tokens? We measure in tokens for billing but our gateway does requests per second.
01:56 Priya Nair: Right, you can express policies in both request/sec and token-based quotas. The Console normalizes them and shows estimated cost impact.
02:06 Jordan Lee: For multi-tenant use-cases, you can create project keys for each customer. That lets you enforce per-customer quotas and also track cost by project.
02:16 Evan Price: And can we programmatically rotate or revoke keys? We need key rotation hooks for security.
02:21 Priya Nair: Yes, there's an API to rotate keys, revoke, and you can set expiry. Rotation is auditable — entries show who rotated and when in the audit log.
02:31 Carlos Mendoza: About audit logs, do you push them to our SIEM or just retain in Redwood?
02:36 Priya Nair: Both — by default logs are retained in the control plane and you can stream to your SIEM via webhook or S3 export. For Private deployments we'll support direct Kinesis/CloudWatch or on-prem collectors.
02:48 Aisha Rahman: Great. On quotas — what happens when a tenant hits quota? Do we get a 429, or are requests queued? We need deterministic behavior for the app.
02:59 Priya Nair: Policy is configurable. Default is reject with 429 and an explanatory error body. Optionally you can enable graceful degradation: fallback to a cheaper model variant or queue with a short backoff. We don't silently drop requests unless configured.
03:13 Jordan Lee: And we also support hierarchy: org-level caps and then project-level overrides, so you can set a global cap for cost control and tighter per-project quotas for high-risk tenants.
03:24 Nina Patel: Okay, that sounds useful. How do we map our internal tenant IDs to project keys?
03:29 Priya Nair: Many customers map their tenant ID to a Redwood project and create keys per tenant automatically during onboarding. We have SDK snippets in the docs you can plug into your provisioning flow.
03:40 Jordan Lee: Quick detour — pricing note: per-token billing still applies but you can also do reserved commits for Dedicated; rate-limiting helps control overages. We'll send a pricing worksheet after.
03:52 Carlos Mendoza: Understood. We have some concerns about latency if you enable rate limiting and fallback to other models; worried about user-facing delays.
04:03 Priya Nair: Good point. Our Smart Routing can route by latency SLOs and prefer low-latency variants. For POC we can benchmark with your sample traces to measure the actual added tail latency.
04:15 Aisha Rahman: Excellent — we'll share a redacted traces file.
04:19 Jordan Lee: Priya, can you show a live example of creating a policy and attaching to project?
04:24 Speaker 2 (Priya): Sure — navigating to Policies -> New Policy -> name it 'MedSphere-defaults'. Show set steady limit 10 req/s, burst 100 req/min, token quota 1M/day. Save. Now attach to Org 'MedSphere-Prod' and optionally to Project 'Tenant-123'.
04:44 Evan Price: When attached, will existing keys immediately pick up the policy or is there a propagation delay?
04:50 Priya Nair: It's near real-time; changes propagate within seconds to the serving plane, though in extremely heavy cached setups could be a minute.
04:58 Carlos Mendoza: You mentioned webhook alarms — can they trigger auto-scaling or notify our ops?
05:04 Priya Nair: They can post to your webhook with payloads summarizing usage and thresholds; many customers wire that into a lambda to trigger autoscale or create incidents.
05:12 Nina Patel: Can we test policies in dry-run? We don't want to accidentally block customers during tuning.
05:17 Priya Nair: Yes — dry-run mode logs what would have been enforced and adds annotations in the audit trail but does not reject traffic.
05:25 Jordan Lee: Quick Q from sales side: does your identity provider sync to our RBAC?
05:30 Carlos Mendoza: Yeah we need SSO integration.
05:33 Priya Nair: We support SAML/Okta and SCIM provisioning. Roles map to Console permissions, and you can restrict who can change policies.
05:41 Aisha Rahman: For Private deployments, what's the footprint? We'd probably use our own KMS for keys.
05:47 Jordan Lee: For Private we ship a control plane you run in your VPC and we support Cloud KMS/HSM integrations. We'll add details in the security pack.
05:56 Carlos Mendoza: Good. Any mention of data residency? We need EU storage for EU tenants.
06:01 Priya Nair: You can choose region and we support data residency via region-specific deploys. We'll capture this in the compliance doc.
06:08 Jordan Lee: Ok let's jump to API examples — Priya will show a curl for token-based quota checks.
06:12 Speaker 2 (Priya): Sharing code now. Example: curl POST /v1/requests with header x-redwood-key: <project-key> and see 200/429 responses. Also show SDK call for rotating keys.
06:28 Aisha Rahman: The SDK link in the docs — is it in Python/Node?
06:31 Priya Nair: We have client libs for Python, Node, and Go, and examples for rotation and provisioning.
06:36 Jordan Lee: A couple of objections that come up — how do you compare to e.g. OpenAI or AWS?
06:40 Carlos Mendoza: Yeah from our CTO perspective we need the control surface more than a pure provider.
06:45 Priya Nair: We position Redwood as inference-first with multi-tenant controls and strong operational features — the goal is predictable economics and per-tenant visibility which is not trivial on other vendor APIs.
06:55 Evan Price: About quotas — can we have soft quotas that bill overage vs hard quotas that block?
07:00 Priya Nair: Yes both. Soft quotas can continue to serve and tag overage for billing; hard quotas will reject. You can also set rate-limits to degrade to cheaper model for cost control.
07:13 Nina Patel: For the POC, can you run a test that simulates 100 tenants with variable usage patterns?
07:19 Jordan Lee: Absolutely. We'll scope that in the SOW — typical POC simulates tenants and shows cost and tail latency.
07:25 Carlos Mendoza: Can we get more detail on encryption in transit and at rest? Also log retention windows.
07:32 Priya Nair: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys. Retention is configurable; default 90 days for control plane logs but can be extended. We'll include specifics in the security pack.
07:44 Aisha Rahman: Another concern — our app gateway does rate-limiting today, we'd like Redwood limits to be a safety net not the primary throttling layer. Will that cause double throttling?
07:56 Priya Nair: Good question — we recommend the gateway be primary and Redwood as secondary. We can add headers in responses to indicate remaining quota so the gateway can surface to users before hitting Redwood limit.
08:10 Jordan Lee: We're about to wrap but one last demo: show the billing by project dashboard.
08:14 Speaker 2 (Priya): Here is usage by project with cost estimates; you can filter by date and export CSV. Also show alerts view where you can set thresholds at 80% of quota.
08:27 Carlos Mendoza: Nice. So next steps recap?
08:30 Jordan Lee: I'll send pricing + SOW, Priya will send security/compliance pack and example rate-limit policy JSON, and MedSphere will share redacted traces and confirm POC dataset. We'll schedule POC kickoff for week of 10/20.
08:45 Aisha Rahman: Sounds good. One last nit — can you include example error payloads for 429 and for degraded responses?
08:52 Priya Nair: Yes we'll include the error schema in the docs.
09:00 Jordan Lee: Great thanks everyone. Any final questions?
09:05 Carlos Mendoza: None from me, thank you.
09:07 Nina Patel: Thanks, bye.
09:09 Jordan Lee: Bye.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker mislabels and small recognition errors (e.g., 'r/s' becomes 'ours', 'KMS' sometimes 'K M S') are present.
